Flood entered Bhote Koshi from Tibetan side around 9 am Wednesday

Timure and Syabrubesi damaged, including Timure Customs Office area

High alert issued downstream to Muglin, covering Nuwakot, Dhading, Gorkha and Chitwan

Authorities urged closure of Prithvi and Tribhuvan highways in risk zones

Cause under investigation - possible glacial lake outburst flood (GLOF)

Extent of casualties and damage still being assessed

A huge and sudden flood entered the Bhote Koshi River from the Chinese side on Wednesday morning, causing major damage in parts of Rasuwa and prompting authorities to issue high-alert warnings downstream as far as Muglin.

Related Articles Rasuwa flood: Security forces, helicopters mobilised for rescue Prithvi Highway in Dhading resumes two-way traffic after landslide

Officials said the flood caused significant damage in Timure and Syabrubesi, with the Timure Customs Office area also affected. The Flood Forecasting Division reported being informed around 9:00 am that a major flood had entered the river from the Tibetan side.

"The flood is unprecedented and huge," an official said, noting damage in Gosaikunda Rural Municipality-2, Timure, and Ward No. 5, Syabrubesi.

By A Staff Reporter, Kathmandu, Aug. 26: Vice President Ramsahay Prasad Yadav has extended greetings to Muslims in Nepal and abroad on the occasion of the birth anniversary of Prophet Muhammad, observed as Muhammad Day.

Issuing a press statement, Vice President Yadav expressed the belief that the occasion inspires people to follow the path of truth, tolerance, good conduct, compassion and social harmony.

He said the teachings of Prophet Muhammad promote the values of humanity, religious harmony, brotherhood, justice and equality.

Yadav noted that Nepal is a multi-ethnic, multi-lingual, multi-religious and multicultural country. He said religious and cultural festivals celebrated across the country contribute to strengthening social relations, national unity and cultural harmony.

According to the Vice President, Muhammad Day is not only a religious occasion but also carries significant social, cultural and moral importance.

He highlighted the tradition among Muslims of observing the occasion through Quran recitation, prayers and other religious practices aimed at self-purification, discipline and spiritual reflection.

Yadav said the teachings of Prophet Muhammad encourage people to speak the truth, act with integrity, support others in times of suffering, forgive mistakes and practice tolerance.

He also emphasised the importance of developing compassion and a spirit of support toward the poor, helpless, orphans and disadvantaged communities.

The Vice President expressed hope that Muhammad Day would help spread the message of religious tolerance, mutual goodwill, social unity and brotherhood. He further wished that the life and teachings of Prophet Muhammad would continue to inspire society to pursue truth, justice, service and dedication.

title: Suspected glacial lake outburst triggers catastrophic flood in Nepal - Everest Chronicle
description: Suspected glacial lake outburst triggers catastrophic flood in Nepal  Everest Chronicle
publisher.title: Everest Chronicle
full_article:
A catastrophic flash flood surged down the Bhotekoshi River on Wednesday morning, wreaking widespread destruction across Rasuwa district and prompting emergency alerts for downstream communities as far as Narayanghat. Local residents described the deluge, which struck around 8 am, as one of the most severe floods in recent decades.

Authorities suspect the disaster may have been triggered by a glacial lake outburst upstream in Tibet. Rasuwa Chief District Officer Narendra Pariyar noted that there was no rainfall in the district headquarters at the time of the flooding, pointing to an upstream event as the likely cause.

The floodwaters are believed to have swept through the historic town of Betrabati and caused extensive damage in Timure and Syafrubesi. Videos circulating on social media show scenes of heavy devastation, with floodwaters raging through settlements and infrastructure.

Emergency alerts have been issued for communities along the Trishuli River, including Trishuli, Galchi, Batarey, and extending down to Narayanghat. Authorities in five districts—Rasuwa, Nuwakot, Dhading, Gorkha, and Chitwan—have urged residents to move to safer locations.

The flood has severely impacted tourism, with thousands of trekkers on the Langtang route affected, particularly those heading towards Gosaikunda. Multiple hydropower projects along the Bhotekoshi River have been swept away or severely damaged. According to the Independent Energy Producers’ Association, Nepal, over ten projects have been affected, with production halted at facilities including the 111-MW Rasuwagadhi, Chilime, and Trishuli-3A hydropower projects.

The Rasuwagadhi border point—a vital trade route with China—has been disrupted. With the Dashain festival approaching, the disruption is expected to severely impact the supply of goods. Finance Minister Swarnim Wagle is leading a high-level team coordinating with the Timure Customs Office on response efforts.

The exact cause of the flood and the full extent of the damage remain under investigation.

Nepal PM Balen Shah Won’t Remove His Sunglasses In Parliament. Here’s Why

Published By : Pragati Ratti

, News18.com

Last Updated: August 26, 2026, 11:50 IST

The Federal Parliament Secretariat has cleared Shah to wear his signature shades inside the House after his office submitted a medical report

Nepal Prime Minister Balen Shah.

Nepal Prime Minister Balendra “Balen" Shah is set to enter Parliament with the one accessory that has become almost inseparable from his public image: his trademark dark sunglasses. And this time, he has a medical reason to keep them on.

The Federal Parliament Secretariat has cleared Shah to wear his signature shades inside the House after his office submitted a medical report recommending that he use sunglasses because he experiences discomfort while looking at bright light. The exemption comes just days after Speaker Dol Prasad Aryal had asked lawmakers to stop wearing dark glasses during parliamentary proceedings.

The controversy is therefore not simply about a pair of sunglasses. For Shah, the glasses have become part of his political identity.

Why Does Balen Shah Need Sunglasses In Parliament?

Shah recently underwent an eye examination at Birendra Military Hospital in Kathmandu after complaining of difficulty seeing in bright light.

According to reports, ophthalmologist Associate Professor Lieutenant Colonel Dr Sachit Dhakal recommended that the prime minister use sunglasses as required and also prescribed eye drops when necessary. Shah’s office subsequently forwarded the medical report and the doctors’ recommendation to the Federal Parliament Secretariat.

Parliament Secretariat spokesperson Ekaram Giri said the documents established that Shah had a medical reason for wearing the glasses, specifically noting his “discomfort seeing in bright light".

Deputy spokesman Ananta Prasad Koirala put it more directly, “A report has been submitted to the secretariat pointing to medical reasons for the respected prime minister to need sunglasses." He added that Shah would be allowed to wear them if they were medically necessary in bright light.

So, while Shah is not necessarily making a personal declaration that he will defy Parliament’s dress expectations, the medical exemption effectively means he can retain the glasses during House proceedings.

Why Were Sunglasses Banned In Nepal Parliament?

The issue began earlier this month when Speaker Aryal instructed party whips to ensure lawmakers did not wear dark sunglasses inside the chamber.

The Speaker said the practice had repeatedly drawn questions and criticism, and Parliament decided that dark glasses would not be permitted during proceedings except when there was a medical reason.

Shah is scheduled to face lawmakers on August 26 in a direct question-and-answer session – his first such appearance under the House of Representatives’ rules since becoming Prime Minister. Eleven lawmakers have registered questions for him.

That appearance also comes amid criticism of Shah’s attendance in Parliament. The Speaker had earlier directed him to appear before the House after lawmakers raised concerns over his absence from parliamentary sittings.

Balen’s Sunglasses: More Than Just Eyewear

For the 36-year-old rapper-turned-politician, the rectangular black shades have been a defining part of his persona since his days as Kathmandu mayor.

Shah was rarely seen without them during his political rise. Often paired with his all-black outfits, the sunglasses became closely associated with his image as an outsider challenging Nepal’s traditional political establishment.

For now, however, the argument has been settled on medical grounds. Balen Shah can walk into Nepal’s Parliament wearing the sunglasses that have followed him from Kathmandu’s streets to the prime minister’s office. And when he faces lawmakers, the country will be watching not just what he says, but whether the man behind those dark glasses finally opens up to Parliament.

title: Bhotekoshi flood: What we know, what remains unclear - The Kathmandu Post
description: Bhotekoshi flood: What we know, what remains unclear  The Kathmandu Post
publisher.title: The Kathmandu Post
full_article:
A massive flash flood struck Rasuwa district early Wednesday, damaging settlements and infrastructure along the Bhotekoshi river and prompting a major search-and-rescue operation. Here is what we know so far:

What happened, and where?

A flash flood swept through the Bhotekoshi river in northern Nepal early Wednesday.

The flood caused extensive damage in Rasuwa district, particularly along settlements bordering the river. Chameli Gurung, deputy chair of Uttargaya Rural Municipality, said around a dozen settlements had been affected, including Syaphrubesi, Betrawati, Mailung, Salletar, Shantibazar, Pairebesi, Khalti Basti, Sole, Trishuli and Battar.

What is known about the damage?

Authorities have yet to release a confirmed toll of deaths, injuries or property damage.

But preliminary information from local officials, residents and security agencies, along with photographs and videos from the affected areas, points to significant destruction. Market areas, particularly Syaphrubesi, appear to have suffered some of the heaviest damage.

Nine Armed Police Force personnel deployed in Timure, near the Nepal-China border, have been reported missing after the flood reached the area at around 9am.

Abi Narayan Kafle, spokesperson for Nepal Police, said the Area Police Office in Timure, the police post in Syaphrubesi and the police post at Rasuwagadhi had also been damaged.

What is the government doing?

The government has deployed two Nepali Army helicopters for search and rescue operations. An emergency meeting is under way at the Home Ministry.

Prime Minister Balendra Shah has also called a meeting to discuss the flooding and the government response.

Authorities have urged residents along the Trishuli river to move to safer areas as the flood moves downstream.

The government has mobilised the Nepali Army, Armed Police Force and Nepal Police for rescue and relief operations, with additional personnel being sent from other districts, Shah said.

The National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority has been activated, while medical teams, Scouts and the Red Cross have been asked to coordinate relief efforts. More ambulances and medical personnel are also being deployed.

A massive flash flood in the Himalayan nation of ​Nepal washed away villages and project sites in ‌a region bordering Tibet, authorities said ​on Wednesday (August 26, 2026), warning of heavy casualties ⁠as they urged those living on river banks to seek higher ground.

The areas of Syapru Besi and ‌Timure in the mountainous district of Rasuwa were severely affected, government officials said, ‌while calling for extra vigilance by ‌residents ⁠along the Bhote Koshi river.

"We have reports ⁠of villages and infrastructure project sites being washed away," district administrator Narendra Pariyar told Reuters, adding that no ​immediate estimates of casualties ‌or property losses were available.

"There could be heavy casualties or loss of property," he said. "But I cannot say for sure now."

Prime ‌Minister Balendra Shah said rescue and ​relief teams, as well as police and the military had been dispatched ⁠to help in the aid effort.

"Instructions have been given ... to move the people living in the ‌lower areas to safer places," he said.

"People along the river are advised to exercise extra caution and remain alert," the government said in its statement.

The Bhote Koshi river originates in Tibet and empties ‌into Nepal's Trishuli river that eventually flows into India ​as the Gandak river.

A flood last year in the Bhote Koshi river killed ⁠nine people, with 24 missing, and washed away ⁠the 'Friendship Bridge' linking Nepal and China to disrupt transport and trade for several months.

That ‌flood was triggered by the draining of a supraglacial lake in Tibet, a ​regional climate monitor said.
